gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 concerns admissibility of solution-adapted test functions in V_h^c and the required relation between c and the solution. It does not diagnose either I001 defect: the unjustified Gauss–Green/boundary-trace use for arbitrary measurable sets or the unsupported h-uniform O(epsilon) estimate for the L1 gradient norm. Its c-dependent repair does not establish the missing finite-perimeter hypothesis or the h-dependent approximation tolerance.

ISSUE-005 addresses globally patching competitors and interfaces across distinct one-dimensional solution pieces and wave curves. I003 instead concerns the classification of background cells whose transition strips are present without the exact shock, and the missing entropy estimate for those strip-only cells. The global wave-curve repair in ISSUE-005 does not recognize or bound this separate class of cells.

Both entries identify that the solution-adapted comparison function used in the minimizer bound is not guaranteed to belong to V_h^c because the theorem imposes no relation between c and the solution amplitude and gradient bounds. Both specifically identify the invalid substitution for small c and repair it by choosing c sufficiently large, with the prediction explicitly extending the condition to all comparison constructions.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The fixed admissibility constraint defining V_h^c is not shown to contain the solution-adapted test/interpolant functions; consequently the minimizer comparison inequality cannot be applied unless c is chosen with sufficient solution-dependent amplitude and gradient margin.

component_coverage.gold_component: The stability test approximating u may lie outside V_h^c because no hypothesis relates c to the solution amplitude and gradient.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that c is arbitrary, that the interpolant requires a solution-dependent lower bound, and that the comparison is inadmissible for small c.

component_coverage.gold_component: The same admissibility gap affects the other solution-adapted comparison functions and leaves the convergence arguments unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies the same gap across the rarefaction, compound, birth, one-dimensional, and multidimensional constructions and proposes c>=C_0(u) based on the relevant amplitude and local construction constants.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns an unsupported logarithmic convergence rate and the balance of rarefaction and shifted-trace errors. I005 concerns the missing nonnegativity of the entropy loss component, caused by using a bare supremum, and the resulting inability to extract residual and initial-trace bounds. The rate repair in ISSUE-003 does not recognize the sign/positive-part defect.

Both entries identify the lateral boundary flux produced by the cellwise divergence-theorem identity, explain that the network is unconstrained at the lateral boundary so the term is uncontrolled, and state that the stability estimate therefore does not follow. Both provide the specific repair of adding a boundary penalty or boundary restriction and retaining/bounding the lateral term.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The lateral boundary flux term does not cancel and is not controlled by the stated loss because the competing network need not satisfy the exact solution's boundary behavior; omitting it invalidates the final-time stability identities and error estimates.

component_coverage.gold_component: The divergence-theorem cancellation leaves a lateral boundary flux term that is absent from the old identity.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly writes the lateral boundary integral arising after summing cellwise identities and contrasts it with the claimed cancellation.

component_coverage.gold_component: Compact support of the exact solution does not constrain the network there, so the lateral term has uncontrolled size and sign and invalidates the stability estimates.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that only the exact solution is boundary-vanishing, gives an uncontrolled O(1) boundary contribution, and identifies the resulting failure of all L1 error estimates.

component_coverage.gold_component: A lateral boundary penalty or boundary restriction must be added and the term retained in each integration-by-parts identity.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction supplies the specific boundary penalty or vanishing-network repair and requires inclusion and control of the lateral term in every identity.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 concerns incompatibility when a single shock traverses multiple one-dimensional solution pieces and requires global patching along that wave curve. I007 concerns several distinct shock branches lying in one multidimensional background cell despite h^2 separation, so one transition layer and the per-cell affine prescription cannot represent or conform to all branches. The global one-dimensional piece-patching diagnosis does not recognize this multidimensional multi-branch-per-cell obstruction.
